title: Temporal Tables
description: Use system-versioned temporal tables to keep automatic row history and query data as it looked at any point in time.

data.text: A system-versioned temporal table keeps the current rows in the main table and automatically writes the previous version of every updated or deleted row into a paired history table. You get row-level history without triggers, audit columns, or a custom archiving job. SQL Server 2016 introduced the feature; Azure SQL Database and SQL Server 2017+ added retention policies.

data.caption: SQL Server moves the old row version into the history table on every update or delete; the main table always holds current rows.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    DML["UPDATE or DELETE\non dbo.Employee"] --> CUR["Current table\ndbo.Employee"]
    CUR -->|old row version| HIST["History table\ndbo.EmployeeHistory"]
    CUR -->|row removed or replaced| DONE["Main table keeps\nonly current rows"]
    Q1["FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF"] --> CUR
    Q1 --> HIST
    Q2["FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL"] --> CUR
    Q2 --> HIST
    HIST --> RET["Retention policy\ndeletes old history"]

data.text: Two `datetime2` columns marked `GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START` and `ROW END` define the period of validity, and `PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME` ties them together. `SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON` creates the history table automatically if you do not name one.

data.title: System-versioned employee table
data.content: The history table must have the same columns, in the same order, with the period columns included.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE dbo.Employee
(
    EmployeeId INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    Name       NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Department NVARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,
    ValidFrom  DATETIME2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START NOT NULL
        CONSTRAINT DF_Employee_ValidFrom DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME(),
    ValidTo    DATETIME2 GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW END NOT NULL
        CONSTRAINT DF_Employee_ValidTo DEFAULT '9999-12-31 23:59:59.9999999',
    PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (ValidFrom, ValidTo)
)
WITH
(
    SYSTEM_VERSIONING = ON (HISTORY_TABLE = dbo.EmployeeHistory)
);

data.text: Query Data as of a Point in Time

data.title: FOR SYSTEM_TIME variants
data.content: `AS OF` returns a single snapshot, `BETWEEN` returns every version whose validity overlaps the range, and `ALL` returns current plus history rows.
data.code:
-- The table as it looked at the start of 2024
SELECT *
FROM dbo.Employee
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF '2024-01-01';

-- Every version that was valid at some point during 2024
SELECT *
FROM dbo.Employee
FOR SYSTEM_TIME BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31';

-- Current rows plus all historical versions
SELECT *
FROM dbo.Employee
FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL
ORDER BY EmployeeId, ValidFrom;

data.title: Schema changes need versioning turned off
data.text: You cannot add, drop, or alter a column while system versioning is on. Set `SYSTEM_VERSIONING = OFF`, make the same change to both the current and history tables, then turn versioning back on. Plan retention before the history table grows: `HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD = 12 MONTHS` tells SQL Server to purge older history automatically.

data.title: Set a history retention period
data.content: Re-declaring SYSTEM_VERSIONING with the same history table adds a retention policy without losing history.

data.title: Interview angle: temporal vs triggers vs CDC
data.text: Temporal tables answer 'what did this row look like at time T?' and keep the history in the same database. Triggers can do the same thing but add overhead and are easy to get wrong on multi-row statements. CDC captures every change in order for downstream consumers. Reach for temporal when the requirement is auditing or point-in-time querying, and for CDC when the requirement is replication or integration.

data.title: Temporal Tables Key Points
points: System-versioned tables keep current rows in the main table and old versions in a history table.
Define ValidFrom/ValidTo as GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START/END and add PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME.
Query history with FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, BETWEEN, CONTAINED IN, or ALL.
Schema changes require disabling system versioning first.
Use HISTORY_RETENTION_PERIOD to stop history from growing forever.
Temporal tables audit row state; CDC streams every change for integration.
